Brok Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Brok, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Brok began in the late 18th century, with synagogue permission granted in 1855; by 1921, 873 Jews lived in the town, most murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery was established around 1852 on land purchased through community contributions, replacing earlier burials in nearby Ostrów Mazowiecka. In 1895, Rabbi Awraham Jehuda Lejb Kozak - who served the community for 40 years and studied under rabbis from Góra Kalwaria and Kock - was buried here. Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1964. A modern symbolic tombstone now commemorates Rabbi Kozak at the site's center.
